clue.text: Many bring down a greater number by the sword

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
to bring someone down is to lay them low
more means a greater number

explanation.surface: Someone cuts down a larger crowd with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives C, the Roman hundred; 'by' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large two-handed Scottish broadsword.

clue.text: He's fine up 'north; put the cap on him anyway

definitions.meaning: in the north of England an exclamation of approval for something first-rate

definitions.text: put the cap on him anyway
definitions.meaning: the one honoured as the top competitor, given a cap or crown

explanation.surface: A northern compliment for a man who deserves the honour of a cap.
explanation.walkthrough: In northern English speech 'champion!' means excellent or fine; and a sporting winner is the one who gets capped or crowned, so the second half describes the titleholder.
explanation.definitionFit: Champion is northern dialect for splendid, and a winner is honoured by being capped.

clue.text: French finance in a part of S America

parts.note: argent is the French word for money
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about money in France and somewhere in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a country occupying much of southern South America.

clue.text: Marriage as a sporting contest

definitions.meaning: a union of husband and wife, a good pairing

explanation.definitionFit: A wedding pairing is a good match, and a football game is also a match.

clue.text: The engineers' point about mine gives workers a break

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass point
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Army engineers in a mine call a pause so the miners can rest.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; 'gives workers' is padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short rest or interval of relief.

clue.text: Change this back for a fair ride

definitions.meaning: to swap one thing for another

definitions.text: this back for a fair ride
definitions.meaning: adding the word back after this one names a fairground roller coaster

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a little puzzle of its own: put 'back' after the answer and you get SWITCHBACK, an old name for a roller coaster at a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: To change is to swap; a switchback is a fairground roller coaster.

clue.text: Colonial statesman liked a few reforms

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A colonial politician was fond of a handful of reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' looks like a noun the statesman liked but signals rearranging LIKEDAFEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon Wakefield was a British promoter of colonisation in South Australia and New Zealand.

clue.text: Returning in glory to this alpine region.

indicators.note: Returning says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone goes back in triumph to a mountain area.
explanation.walkthrough: The run LORYT sits across 'glory to'; 'in' signals the hiding and 'Returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine area of western Austria and northern Italy.

clue.text: Keeping out of the way of punishment

definitions.meaning: concealing oneself, staying out of sight
a beating, as in giving a child a good thrashing

explanation.definitionFit: Being concealed means staying out of sight; a hiding is also a thrashing.

clue.text: Russian settler takes care of dry goods measure

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the address abbreviation for care of
a peck is a unit for measuring grain and other dry goods

explanation.surface: A Russian colonist looks after a quantity of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settler' means something that settles a bill, a coin, not a colonist; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The copeck is a small Russian coin, and coins settle debts.

clue.text: Anything poetical

parts.note: an old word for anything at all, now found mostly in verse

explanation.definitionFit: Aught is an archaic and literary word meaning anything whatever.

clue.text: So obstructed, a player's unlikely to go to pot

definitions.text: So obstructed, a player's unlikely to go to pot

parts.words: So obstructed, a player's unlikely to go to pot
parts.note: on the green baize a blocked ball cannot be potted, and to go to pot also means to decline

explanation.surface: Someone so blocked at every turn is unlikely to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: To go to pot usually means to deteriorate; here it is potting a ball at the table game when another ball blocks the path.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stymied by a ball in the way at the cue game is the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: With which a joker periodically floors us ?

definitions.text: With which a joker periodically floors us ?

parts.words: With which a joker periodically floors us ?
parts.note: a comedian knocks the audience flat with laughter by the closing line of a gag, as a boxer floors with a blow

explanation.surface: A prankster keeps knocking us down with something.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing line of a joke delivers the laugh, as a blow delivers a knockdown.

clue.text: Look in the marsh for a criminal

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Search the bog for a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone who has committed a serious crime.

clue.text: With no fixture around team could get rusty

indicators.note: around means these pieces go round the other

parts.note: O, nought, means none
a fixture is a match on a set date
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A side without matches may lose its sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rusty' is literal, chemical corrosion, not the out-of-practice sense; 'could' and 'With' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To oxidate is to oxidise, as iron does when it corrodes.

clue.text: Vintage drink of the first water ?

definitions.text: Vintage drink of the first water ?

parts.words: Vintage drink of the first water ?
parts.note: the oldest drink of all, enjoyed by the first man in Eden, is plain water

explanation.surface: A fine old wine of the highest quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the first water' means top quality, but here it is water drunk by the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's wine is a jocular name for water, the only drink in Eden.

clue.text: Emily Bronte's canine retainer

definitions.meaning: the novelist's mastiff, famously devoted to her
a gamekeeper or custodian employed to look after something

explanation.definitionFit: Emily Brontë's dog was named Keeper; a keeper is also a guardian or servant.

clue.text: Get rid of the bird in select company

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the elite are a select group
mina is a spelling of myna, the Asian starling

explanation.surface: Remove the bird from high society.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove it entirely.

clue.text: You can hardly miss the store's entrance !

definitions.text: You can hardly miss the store's entrance !

parts.words: You can hardly miss the store's entrance !
parts.note: the big doorway of a farm storage building is proverbially too large a target to miss

explanation.surface: A shop's front door is impossible to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop but is a farm building for storing hay.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn door is the idiomatic example of a target nobody could miss.

clue.text: Intake of port revealed in Mary Tudor's autopsy

definitions.text: Intake of port revealed in Mary Tudor's autopsy

parts.words: Intake of port revealed in Mary Tudor's autopsy
parts.note: Queen Mary I said that the French town she lost would be found lying in her heart when she was opened after death

explanation.surface: A queen's post-mortem shows she had been drinking fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intake of port' suggests drinking; it is the harbour town captured by France in 1558, which Mary Tudor said would be found written on her heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Channel port was England's last continental possession, lost under Mary I.

clue.text: Impressed, stopped work

definitions.meaning: deeply moved, as in taken by something
went on strike in an industrial dispute

explanation.definitionFit: One who is moved is smitten; workers who walk out have gone on strike.

clue.text: Tipsy-cake ?

parts.note: a sponge named after a fortified wine, as if the cake were drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Madeira cake is a plain sponge traditionally served with the Portuguese island's fortified wine.

clue.text: Couturier could do Times crossword !

indicators.note: crossword suggests the letters of the words are crossed over and jumbled

explanation.surface: A dressmaker boasts of solving the newspaper puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' is a link; the rearranged letters are DOTIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A modiste is a fashionable milliner or dressmaker.

clue.text: The curse, of drink, one might ignorantly shay?

indicators.note: the slurred shay for say suggests a tipsy or untutored speaker pronouncing a word wrongly

parts.note: the swear word, slurred by a drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk mutters that drink is a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: The cherry brandy is often mispronounced like curse; 'shay' mimics drunken speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a clear cherry brandy.

clue.text: Bad performers clapped in these clubs?

definitions.meaning: wrongdoers are clapped in shackles, punning on applause for performers
golf clubs with angled metal heads

explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners are put in fetters; golfers carry metal-headed clubs.

clue.text: It takes eight players, etc, up, into lift

annotationWithheld.why: It takes eight players, etc, up, into lift (5): rev(etc) gives CTE, but no reading of 'lift' supplies O..T around it, so the wordplay cannot be completed
annotationWithheld.clue: It takes eight players, etc, up, into lift

clue.text: What the communist did in editing

parts.note: Red is a common nickname for a communist
what someone did is an action

explanation.surface: A question about a Marxist's role in editing.
explanation.definitionFit: Redaction is the work of preparing a text for publication.

clue.text: Skip the sauce

definitions.meaning: pickled flower buds used in a sauce for mutton

explanation.definitionFit: To skip is to frolic; the pickled bud flavours a classic British sauce served with mutton.

clue.text: Put bits of light entertainment on display

parts.note: to set is to put down
pieces are bits

explanation.surface: Fragments of a show are placed on view.
explanation.definitionFit: Set pieces are showy, elaborately staged scenes in a play or film.

clue.text: A plot involving the' founder 'of the academy

indicators.note: involving suggests the letters are rolled up and turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A scheme concerning the man who set up a college.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek philosopher established the Academy at Athens.

clue.text: Assassins heading the parade?

parts.note: a pop record at number one is a top seller, so those leading the chart line-up could be called this

explanation.surface: Killers lead the procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parade' is the hit parade, the pop chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Hired contract killers; read as a phrase it suggests chart-topping performers.

clue.text: Stingy drink ?

parts.note: near is an old word for mean or tight-fisted
beer is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A mean round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue is a drink stingy with alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Near beer is a low-alcohol malt drink, mean in its strength.
